answer: Each identity registers one ocean sounding station, locking an 80-credit bond. Each epoch it sends a ripple ping and logs the echo time. Any auditor recomputes depth from echo time against the seabed chart and checks the ping against its sonnet pattern of 14 pulses; a missing, duplicate, or mismatched ping burns the bond. One frequency slot per station: first 40 credits, k-th 40+12(k-1), so 1,000 fakes pay 6,034,000 in fees plus 80,000 locked. A rented-sounder ring fails: shared stations share one ping pattern and echo time. An honest operator pays 40 once, bond back after a clean epoch.
